text: Fodor's analysis of the structure of concepts led him to a notoriously 'radical' conclusion about concept acquisition. What was it?
choices: All concepts are learned from perceptual experience by abstraction
Most lexical concepts -- even ones like CARBURETOR or MICROWAVE -- are innate, merely triggered rather than learned, because unstructured primitive concepts cannot be learned by definition
Concepts are prototypes, stored as statistical summaries of experienced instances
Concepts are patterns of sensorimotor activation grounded in the body
explanation: Because Fodor held that most concepts are primitive (unstructured), and that learning a concept requires assembling it from simpler ones, he inferred that primitive concepts must be innate -- radical concept nativism, widely treated as a reductio yet resting on an unanswered challenge about concept learning. Option 0 is concept empiricism; option 2 is prototype theory; option 3 is Barsalou's grounded cognition -- all rivals to Fodor's nativism.
